candidate.title: snRNA-seq
candidate.scope: The snRNA-seq row of the assigned Illumina poster crop: a single-nuclei RNA-to-cDNA library architecture from cell suspension through indexed enrichment-ready DNA fragments. Its explicit route is cell lysis/centrifugation, nuclei sorting, first-strand synthesis, cDNA synthesis, PCR, tagmentation, and gap repair/PCR. The Single cell to RNA/AA(n) vignette identifies the analyte; the separated supernatant is a noncontinuing fraction. Nearby NanoCAGE/CAGEscan, Smart-seq2 and FRISCR rows and the right-hand dimethyl-sulfate chemical legend are contextual, not alternative targets or reagents of this row. This is a poster-level architecture, not an assertion that all snRNA-seq implementations use identical preparation or that the later catalogue implementation is the complete poster-cited protocol.

operations.label: Lyse and centrifuge
operations.description: Disrupt the cells in the suspension and separate the nuclei-containing fraction from the supernatant. The nuclei fraction continues to sorting; the supernatant has no depicted onward route.
operations.mechanism: Cell lysis followed by centrifugal separation, represented as one named block.
operations.information_effect: Selects the nuclear compartment as the RNA source rather than retaining whole-cell contents. This physical enrichment does not establish perfect purity.

operations.label: Sort nuclei
operations.description: Select nuclei from the separated nuclei fraction for the single-nucleus RNA workflow. The selected nuclear material, rather than the supernatant, enters first-strand synthesis.
operations.information_effect: Retains the single-nucleus origin of the subsequent library at schematic scope. Sorting hardware and collection compartments are not drawn in this row.

operations.label: First strand synthesis
operations.description: Copy accessible RNA from the sorted nuclei into a first cDNA strand, producing the paired-strand intermediate shown with an adaptor-linked T-rich region opposite the RNA A-rich region and a CCC-labelled end.
operations.mechanism: The A-rich/T-rich pairing supports poly(A)-associated, oligo(dT)-primed reverse transcription at schematic level. No separate nucleus-opening operation is drawn between sorting and this block.
operations.information_effect: Transfers captured nuclear transcript sequence into DNA; the A/T interface indicates a poly(A)-associated sampling route rather than an unbiased census of nuclear RNA.

operations.information_effect: Establishes end handles for amplification of RNA-derived cDNA while retaining transcript insert sequence.

method_scopes.rationale: All listed local operations belong to the explicitly labelled snRNA-seq row and connect through its arrows and intermediate drawings. Single-nuclei RNA sequencing is the expanded name, not a second target. The poster lists Grindberg 2013; its matched abstract establishes the core single-nucleus mRNA-to-cDNA assay. The same-target collection page instead describes Lacar 2016, whose full text supports a later implementation and a compatible downstream tagmentation/indexing interface. That implementation sits within snRNA-seq but does not establish universal use of C1, Smart-seq2, LNA oligos or any unshown sample processing. The neighbouring Smart-seq2 row remains outside this record, even though Smart-seq2 is a component in one of Lacar's preparations.

unknowns.question: Does the poster-cited Grindberg 2013 implementation use precisely the depicted CCC/GGG cDNA interface and indexed tagmentation route? Its supplied abstract verifies single-nucleus mRNA-to-cDNA transcriptomics, not these detailed interfaces. Original Methods/Supporting Information would be needed to verify that paper-specific correspondence; the diagram itself establishes the scoped route, and the later Lacar full text is not substituted for the original implementation.

checks.rationale: The candidate covers the assigned snRNA-seq row in both directions: cell-suspension fractionation, retained-nuclei sorting, RNA-to-cDNA conversion, cDNA synthesis, PCR, tagmentation, and the indexed final fragment. Its only multi-output operation is the depicted fractionation, with nuclei continuing and supernatant terminating; no independent processing branches are collapsed. All state/operation/flow interfaces preserve the nuclear origin and DNA readout carrier. The left RNA vignette is acknowledged without manufacturing an extracted-RNA transfer into the cell suspension. Adjacent methods and the chemical legend are excluded. Paper associations and abstract-versus-full-text limits are explicit. Acceptance is for the declared poster-level architecture; the candidate does not claim verification of Grindberg's complete reaction sequence.
